verdict: HBM to double again in 2027 (TrendForce); hyperscaler capex revised to $720-745B; NVDA at record; COHR/LITE surge on Chinese transceiver ban; correction risk post-2026 confirmed as capacity ramp now visible.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (last 24-72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Pricing:** TrendForce (Oct 4) forecasts HBM ASPs to rise ~121% in 2027; a 12-layer/36 GB HBM4 stack projected to go from ~$600 today to ~$1,300 next year. Conventional DRAM: Samsung seeking up to 20% QoQ increase for Q3-2026. Micron noted nearly all 2027 HBM supply quotas are allocated. Memflation remains in hyperdrive.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp / Correction Risk:** Micron doubling HBM capacity to ~100K wafer starts/month by end-2026. Samsung targeting ~250K WPM by year-end; SK Hynix M15X fab ramping since Q1-2026. All three suppliers certifying HBM4 for NVIDIA Vera Rubin per Silicon Analysts tracker. Correction-risk signal **alive**: massive capacity additions now visibly completing, pointing to 2027 pricing pressure as baseline warned.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler AI Capex:** Combined 2026 guidance from top-4 hyperscalers revised up to **$720-745B** (from ~$600-700B baseline). Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta all raised capex in latest earnings round; Microsoft's apparent reduction is an accounting change per tmtfinance. No guide-downs visible. CreditSights sees ~75% AI-directed.

**Signal 4 — AMD MI400/Custom ASIC:** Google reportedly tapping AMD to design a next-gen TPU with on-package CPU cores for RL workloads (SemiAnalysis, unconfirmed). AMD MI400/Helios H2-2026 on track: 72 MI455X accelerators, 31 TB aggregate HBM4, EPYC Venice + Pensando Vulcano networking. No fresh Oct 7-8 AMD confirmation. Custom silicon (AVGO, Google TPU, AWS Trainium) remains the larger structural NVDA threat per analysts.

**Signal 5 — Optical/Photonics:** Major moves around Oct 1 (7 days): **COHR +10%** on PhotonLink AI datacenter optics platform launch (20+ active engagements) and Bernstein Outperform initiation; **LITE +9%**; CIEN rallied. Catalysts: (a) Bernstein bullish sector call, (b) US lawmakers introduced bill prohibiting federal use of Chinese optical transceivers (targets Eoptolink, Zhongji Innolight) — Morgan Stanley sees 3.2T modules as starting point. This is a genuine positive structural inflection for US optical names. InP demand confirmed tight; CPO volume window remains 2027-2028 per LightCounting.

**Signal 6 — Solar:** Section 232 tariffs signed Aug 6, effective Dec 4, 2026: price floors $0.38/W (modules), $0.22/W (cells), plus 15% ad valorem on polysilicon derivatives. FSLR facing elevated US panel inventory + 15% tariff headwind per Yahoo Finance (Oct 1). USITC injury vote on India/Indonesia/Laos AD/CVD **Oct 14** — watch for FSLR/NXT read-through. AI datacenter power demand structural positive intact, but near-term FSLR overhang is real. ENPH, NXT, ARRY: no fresh news this window.

**Signal 7 — Watchlist Catalysts:** See Watchlist Movers below.

## Context vs. Baseline

- Hyperscaler capex has exceeded the baseline $600-700B range — now tracking $720-745B+ — a bullish incremental read vs. May baseline.
- HBM pricing trajectory for 2027 (doubling again) is incrementally MORE bullish than baseline for MU/SK Hynix/Samsung near-term, but simultaneously **confirms the correction-risk setup** as capacity completions are now visibly happening.
- Optical sector is having a standout October: the Chinese transceiver restriction legislation is a new structural catalyst not in the baseline.
- Solar: Section 232 implementation and inventory glut are new near-term headwinds for FSLR vs. baseline.

## Most Important Development

**HBM prices forecast to ~double again in 2027** (TrendForce Oct 4): a 12-layer HBM4 stack projected at ~$1,300 by next year. Combined with the $720-745B hyperscaler capex revision and NVDA hitting an all-time high this week, the near-term bull case remains intact — but the capacity ramp by all three HBM suppliers through year-end 2026 keeps the post-2026 correction risk squarely on the radar.
